query: Consider the following context: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for next-generation nuclear applications, particularly fusion reactors, due to their excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance. In that context, which material can be used for low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with the addition of low-activation elements (e.g., W, V, Ti) can be used as low-activation structural materials for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors.
generation.intervention: Addition of low-activation elements (e.g., W, V, Ti) to refractory HEAs
generation.conditions: High-temperature, irradiated environment of fusion reactors
generation.mechanism: Improved irradiation resistance and high-temperature mechanical properties due to the addition of low-activation elements
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced low-activation and high-temperature resistance properties
generation.baseline: Traditional alloys with insufficient high-temperature mechanical properties or irradiation resistance
generation.boundary: Limited by the availability of low-activation elements and their compatibility with refractory HEAs
generation.uncertainty: The exact effect of the addition of low-activation elements on the properties of refractory HEAs is uncertain and requires further research

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of the high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance of refractory HEAs with and without the addition of low-activation elements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of low-activation elements does not result in improved high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance, the hypothesis is falsified
